concept.setting: a tauren village on golden rolling grassland under a vast open sky, gentle hills and mesas on the horizon, warm late-afternoon light, smoke rising from cookfires
concept.buildings: large conical and domed tents and round longhouses of painted hide stretched over thick log frames, the frame poles crossing and sticking out at the peak, hides painted with bold geometric bands and zigzags, broad low doorways with hide flaps, wooden decks and ramps on stout posts, carved wooden totems at the corners, feathers, horns and bone trim, everything big, sturdy and rounded to suit huge folk
concept.landmark: a great tall totem pole of stacked carved animal heads with painted wings spread at the top, beside a wind-rider tower: a tall wooden lookout with a round hide-roofed platform and roosts for winged mounts
concept.street_life: cookfires and drying racks, kodo beast pens with log fences, woven baskets and clay pots, drums, hide banners on tall poles, stone circles, totems along a wide dirt path
concept.greenery: tall golden grass and scattered wildflowers, a few lone trees, hay bales
concept.materials: spruce and oak logs for frames and totems, oak and birch planks for decks, white, yellow, orange-brown and brown wool and terracotta for painted hide, red and light blue accents in the painted bands, bone blocks and bone trim, hay bales, mud bricks and packed mud for hearths, campfires, lanterns
concept.ground: golden grass and a wide dirt path

tavern.what: the village's great lodge (its tavern): one big single-storey hall under a broad hide roof, a long feast table and casks round a central hearth, three small sleeping alcoves for guests each opening off the hall, a hide banner over the door
tavern.form: A long hide hall on a 20 x 16 plot (5 x 4 tiles of 4 blocks): the hall about 17 x 11, a stepped barrel vault of hide from a low skirt to a ridge about 10-11 blocks up, rounded at both ends like a long tent (never a gable), log ribs arching over it and crossing above the ridge, a deck in front on totem posts under a deep hide awning, the front closed by a hide wall with one broad door in the middle. The hide walls are NOT walls: they lean inward from no more than 2-3 blocks above the ground (a short upright skirt of hide, then stairs stepping in every one or two blocks), so the whole outline is a curve from the ground to the peak. No vertical wall above 3 blocks anywhere, no gable ends, no window rows, no second floor.

workshop_smith.what: a smith's forge tent and home: an open-fronted forge under a hide awning with anvil, quench trough and the smith's job blocks, joined at the back to a closed round sleeping tent with its own door and two beds
workshop_smith.form: A forge tent and a sleeping tent on a 16 x 12 plot (4 x 3 tiles of 4 blocks): at the front, a smithy under a broad hide awning on log posts, walled on three sides and closed at the front by a hide wall with a broad door (no open front: the forge is reached from inside); joined at the back, a closed round sleeping tent with its own inner doorway off the forge. Both leaning hide over log frames, the poles crossing above each peak. The hide walls are NOT walls: they lean inward from no more than 2-3 blocks above the ground (a short upright skirt of hide, then stairs stepping in every one or two blocks), so the whole outline is a curve from the ground to the peak. No vertical wall above 3 blocks anywhere, no gable ends, no window rows, no second floor.

cottage_7x7.what: a family tent: one round-shouldered conical hide tent on a log frame, its frame poles crossing and sticking out above the peak, a broad low doorway under a hide flap with a wooden deck and broad steps in front on log posts, carved totems with bone horns at the deck corners, hay bales and pots, four beds round a central hearth inside
cottage_7x7.form: A single conical tent on a 12 x 12 plot (3 x 3 tiles of 4 blocks): the cone about 9 blocks across at its foot, a stepped cone of hide from a low skirt to a peak about 10-11 blocks up, frame poles crossing above it, the deck and steps in front of the door inside the plot. The hide walls are NOT walls: they lean inward from no more than 2-3 blocks above the ground (a short upright skirt of hide, then stairs stepping in every one or two blocks), so the whole outline is a curve from the ground to the peak. No vertical wall above 3 blocks anywhere, no gable ends, no window rows, no second floor.

house_10x7.what: a family yurt: one broad domed hide yurt on a log frame, the dome ribbed by log poles that cross above the crown, painted bands round its belly, a wide low doorway with a deck and broad steps, carved totems at the front corners, six beds round a hearth inside on one floor
house_10x7.form: A single broad dome tent (a yurt) on a 16 x 12 plot (4 x 3 tiles of 4 blocks): the dome an oval about 13 x 9 at its foot, a low upright hide skirt about 2-3 blocks high, then a stepped dome rising to a crown about 10 blocks up, its log ribs standing proud of the hide and crossing above the crown, a deck and steps at the door. Broader than the cone tent, not much taller. The hide walls are NOT walls: they lean inward from no more than 2-3 blocks above the ground (a short upright skirt of hide, then stairs stepping in every one or two blocks), so the whole outline is a curve from the ground to the peak. No vertical wall above 3 blocks anywhere, no gable ends, no window rows, no second floor.

factions.about: Clans of one race, the same contract as orc, dwarf, goblin and night elf: one canonical palette per clan, the swaps from the authored base; the land chooses which clan settles where (styles/settlement.json). Each clan's `swaps` is its palette expanded to plain block ids for 1.21.1 (generated by src/styles/expand.mjs: read these, not the palette).
factions.base: the authored base materials (tauren parts are built in these and nothing else for frames, hides and trim): spruce logs, wood and planks (and forms) for frames, poles, decks, ramps and totems; the hide's SHAPE (cones, domes, curved roofs, stepped with stairs and slabs) in smooth_sandstone (cream) and sandstone (ochre), each with its stairs and slabs, and mud_bricks (and forms) for tan-brown hide (delivered parts carry no red sandstone: it renders bright orange); painted bands on the hide in full terracotta blocks: white, yellow, brown, red and cyan (turquoise) terracotta, with matching wool, carpet and banners only as small accents; bone_block for horns, tusks and skulls; hay_block; packed_mud for hearths and footings; campfires and lanterns; the yard surface red_sand and dead_bush (markers the placer swaps for the land's ground and plant)
